newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says no new moves to control loan growth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says no new moves to control loan growth.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday the government is not planning any new measures to curb loan growth or consumption.
He told reporters after launching a new ratings agency that the government would continue to rely on measures to encourage savings to control consumption.
"We have set up major committees and programmes to encourage savings...And I think that should be a more positive way," he said.

Bank Negara, the central bank, said in its monthly report on monetary conditions that total loans extended by banking institutions rose by 6.4 billion ringgit, or 2.3 percent, in July, against an increase of 3.2 billion ringgit, or 1.2 percent, in June.
Total deposits grew 6.1 billion ringgit, or 2 percent, in July against an increase of 3.7 billion, or 1.2 percent, in June.
"As the increase in loans outpaced that of deposits, the banking system experienced a small resource gap of 236 million in July (compared with a surplus of 493 million in June)," the Bank said.
As a result, the loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 89.98 percent at the end of July, from 89.5 percent the previous month, the report said.
The Bank also said the annual growth rate of deposits rose to 24.9 percent at the end of July from 22.3 percent the previous month.

Asked if the government planned any new measures to control loans or consumption spending and fight inflation, Anwar said: "Not necessarily. We will continue our programmes to increase the level of savings."

Anwar noted that the Consumer Price Index rose by 3.8 percent year-on-year in July -- the same level of increase as in June. The government has said it aims to keep the annual rate of inflation below four percent. ($1 = 2.5 ringgit)
